query: what must a developer publish or report before deploying a frontier model

stretches.quote: ##### Documentation and transparency are components of risk governance
stretches.note: Section 3.2: publishing pre-deployment test results in a model or system card 'has become common practice'; transparency reports; information sharing via third parties; 'Some regulatory frameworks, such as the EU AI Act or California's… SB 53, mandate information sharing about general-purpose AI risks in some cases'. Voluntary practice described alongside mandates, without the content of any duty.

stretches.quote: ##### Several jurisdictions have introduced laws with transparency requirements
stretches.note: Section 3.2: the Report's description of the legal instruments: EU AI Act (transparency, copyright, safety for GPAI models), the Code of Practice (documentation; for the most advanced models evaluations, risk assessment and mitigation, information security, serious incident reporting), Korea's Framework Act ('high-impact' systems), SB 53 ('transparency requirements on safety frameworks and incident reporting'); 'too early to assess'. Does not set out what must be published.

stretches.quote: #### Organisational risk management, transparency, and risk reporting frameworks
stretches.note: Section 3.2: EU Code as 'a voluntary framework', more than two dozen signatories as of December 2025; HAIP Reporting Framework, at least 20 developers' public transparency reports; China's pledges (17 companies); Seoul commitments (16 developers) to publish Frontier AI Safety Frameworks.

stretches.note: Table 3.4: documentation (model and system cards), incident reporting, risk management frameworks, transparency reports (HAIP), whistleblower protection; each with the Report's one-line account and sources.

stretches.quote: Since the publication of the last Report (January 2025), multiple jurisdictions
stretches.note: Section 3.1 Updates: China, the EU and the US have called for or begun implementing 'safety evaluations and transparency disclosures (such as safety and security protocols and model card releases), whistleblower protections, and incident reporting mechanisms'.

stretches.quote: In addition to funding, data-collection efforts
stretches.note: Section 3.5 Updates: signatories of the EU Code 'commit to systematically tracking, documenting, and reporting serious incidents to the EU AI Office'; 'too early to assess'.

stretches.quote: Since 2023, several frontier AI developers have voluntarily published documents
stretches.note: Frontier AI Safety Frameworks: published voluntarily; most require an initial capabilities evaluation before mitigation and 'a residual risk analysis or a safety case' after; several developers in 2025 reported early-warning alerts or that they could not rule out crossing thresholds and applied heightened safeguards.

What developers do not disclose: training data and development information; 'legitimate reasons' (IP, competitive advantage, security) but nondisclosure 'can also conceal problematic practices'; the gap this leaves for external scrutiny.

stretches.quote: ##### AI development outpaces traditional governance cycles
stretches.note: 'Some current governance approaches use thresholds based on training compute to determine risk management requirements'; inference-time scaling 'may challenge the effectiveness of such thresholds'.
